intro_en:
# Before the first scene: reading Japanese

No audio or prior literacy is assumed. Keep it available beside the story. You can begin reading with the charts; you do not need to memorise them first.

Japanese normally runs without spaces. A kana sign represents a short rhythmic unit called a mora. Some sounds use two signs but still form one mora, such as きゃ (kya). English spellings below are reading aids, not English words. Japanese vowels are approximately a as in father, i as in machine, u with unrounded lips, e as in bed, o as in more without its final glide. English comparisons are approximate; text cannot supply a full pronunciation course.

## Hiragana

| | a | i | u | e | o |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vowel | あ a | い i | う u | え e | お o |
| k | か ka | き ki | く ku | け ke | こ ko |
| s | さ sa | し shi | す su | せ se | そ so |
| t | た ta | ち chi | つ tsu | て te | と to |
| n | な na | に ni | ぬ nu | ね ne | の no |
| h | は ha | ひ hi | ふ fu | へ he | ほ ho |
| m | ま ma | み mi | む mu | め me | も mo |
| y | や ya | — | ゆ yu | — | よ yo |
| r | ら ra | り ri | る ru | れ re | ろ ro |
| w | わ wa | — | — | — | を o (particle) |

ん is its own mora, conventionally written n. Japanese r is a brief tongue tap, not an English r. Modern ordinary words do not require obsolete ゐ or ゑ.

Two small strokes, dakuten, change a consonant. A small circle, handakuten, changes the h row to p.

| | a | i | u | e | o |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| g | が ga | ぎ gi | ぐ gu | げ ge | ご go |
| z | ざ za | じ ji | ず zu | ぜ ze | ぞ zo |
| d | だ da | ぢ ji | づ zu | で de | ど do |
| b | ば ba | び bi | ぶ bu | べ be | ぼ bo |
| p | ぱ pa | ぴ pi | ぷ pu | ぺ pe | ぽ po |

じ and ぢ, and ず and づ, often have the same pronunciation in standard Japanese, but their spelling is not interchangeable. Preserve the spelling you read.

Small ゃ, ゅ, ょ combine with the preceding i-column sign: きゃ kya, きゅ kyu, きょ kyo. The main sets are きゃ/きゅ/きょ, ぎゃ/ぎゅ/ぎょ, しゃ/しゅ/しょ (sha/shu/sho), じゃ/じゅ/じょ (ja/ju/jo), ちゃ/ちゅ/ちょ (cha/chu/cho), にゃ/にゅ/にょ, ひゃ/ひゅ/ひょ, びゃ/びゅ/びょ, ぴゃ/ぴゅ/ぴょ, みゃ/みゅ/みょ and りゃ/りゅ/りょ. Thus きや is ki-ya, two morae; きゃ is kya, one. Small っ marks a held consonant before the next sound: きて (kite) differs from きって (kitte). Do not replace っ with full-size つ.

Long vowels last two morae. Keep written vowels: おおきい is o-o-ki-i. In many ordinary words, おう is pronounced with a long o and えい with a long e, while spelling remains おう and えい. You will meet the exact spelling with each word; do not change it on the basis of the Roman letters.

## Katakana

Katakana commonly writes loanwords, foreign names and emphatic forms. It is another script, not another language. Learn each new word's meaning separately; a loanword need not mean exactly what its source word means.

| | a | i | u | e | o |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vowel | ア a | イ i | ウ u | エ e | オ o |
| k | カ ka | キ ki | ク ku | ケ ke | コ ko |
| s | サ sa | シ shi | ス su | セ se | ソ so |
| t | タ ta | チ chi | ツ tsu | テ te | ト to |
| n | ナ na | ニ ni | ヌ nu | ネ ne | ノ no |
| h | ハ ha | ヒ hi | フ fu | ヘ he | ホ ho |
| m | マ ma | ミ mi | ム mu | メ me | モ mo |
| y | ヤ ya | — | ユ yu | — | ヨ yo |
| r | ラ ra | リ ri | ル ru | レ re | ロ ro |
| w | ワ wa | — | — | — | ヲ (rare) |

ン is n. Voicing uses ガギグゲゴ, ザジズゼゾ, ダヂヅデド, バビブベボ and パピプペポ with the same values as the hiragana rows. Small ャュョ form combinations in the same way; small ッ holds the following consonant. The bar ー lengthens the preceding vowel: コーヒー is ko-o-hi-i. Look carefully at シ/ツ and ソ/ン; use the chart whenever needed. Extra combinations such as ファ fa, フィ fi, フェ fe, フォ fo, ティ ti, ディ di, ウィ wi, ウェ we and ウォ wo occur in loanwords and will be explained with the words that use them.

## Read the first scene's words

| Japanese | Read it | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ゆい | yu-i | Yui, an adult volunteer |
| れん | re-n | Ren, another adult volunteer |
| かさ | ka-sa | umbrella |
| ふだ | fu-da | tag |
| ほん | ho-n | book |
| なまえ | na-ma-e | name |
| あかい | a-ka-i | red |
| あおい | a-o-i | blue |
| おおきい | o-o-ki-i | big |
| ちいさい | chi-i-sa-i | small |
| みます | mi-ma-su | look at / looks at |
| もちます | mo-chi-ma-su | hold / holds |

The story must still establish these meanings at first use through its delivered scene and aids. This guide helps decoding; a list alone does not make a sentence inferable.

Particles are short grammatical words attached to phrases. When は is the topic particle, read wa; the spelling stays は. The direction particle へ is read e, and the object particle を is read o. In other words the same signs may retain their usual sounds. The grammar note explains each particle when the story uses it.

Worked example: ゆいはかさをもちます。 Split for explanation only: ゆい | は | かさ | を | もちます. Read yu-i wa ka-sa o mo-chi-ma-su. It means “Yui holds an umbrella.” The story itself keeps ordinary unspaced Japanese.

Try three recognition questions with the table available, then uncover the answers. (1) Which name ends with ん: ゆい or れん? (2) Which means big: おおきい or ちいさい? (3) In ゆいは, is は read ha or wa? Answers: (1) れん; (2) おおきい; (3) wa, because it is the topic particle. This short decoding practice supplements the chapter's full exercises.

## Later kanji and typing

The opening four chapters use kana. Later, known words acquire kanji spellings with small kana readings above them, called furigana. A compound may need one reading over the whole word. You are not expected to guess a new reading from a character's appearance, and readings do not replace meaning support.

Use a Japanese input method (IME) to type answers. Convert to the taught spelling when a kanji form is requested; otherwise the item explains which variants it accepts. Preserve voicing, small kana and long vowels. Space and final punctuation are presentation differences; か/が and きや/きゃ can distinguish different words. You may consult the charts throughout the course.


## Chapter 1: meanings and first pattern

| Japanese | Reading | Meaning in this scene |
|---|---|---|
| かさ | kasa | umbrella |
| ほん | hon | book |
| ふだ | fuda | tag |
| なまえ | namae | name |
| へや | heya | room |
| いりぐち | iriguchi | entrance |
| あおい | aoi | blue |
| あかい | akai | red |
| おおきい | ōkii | big |
| ちいさい | chiisai | small |
| みます | mimasu | look-at |
| もちます | mochimasu | hold |
| これ | kore | this |
| だれ | dare | who |
| どれ | dore | which |
| ちがいます | chigaimasu | differ |
| は | wa (particle) | topic particle (read wa) |
| を | o (particle) | object particle (read o) |
| の | no | possession or affiliation |
| です | desu | is; polite identification |
| ではありません | de wa arimasen | is not; polite negative identification |
| か | ka | question particle |
| いいえ | iie | no |
| さん | san | respectful name suffix |
| どうぞ | dōzo | here you are; offering something |
| ありがとうございます | arigatō gozaimasu | thank you |

へや is a room; いりぐち is its entrance. Yui and Ren are looking at two umbrellas, their name cards, and two books. Start with the chart available. ゆいはかさをもちます means “Yui holds an umbrella.” れんのかさです means “It is Ren’s umbrella.” ゆいのかさではありません means “It is not Yui’s umbrella.” A tag may belong to one person without the umbrella belonging to that person. The story will show why that distinction matters.


## Before Chapter 2: a room and its owner

かばん (kaban) means bag; it is shown on the chair in the room scene.

| Japanese | Meaning in this chapter |
|---|---|
| ここ | here |
| そこ | there |
| あそこ | over-there |
| どこ | where |
| つくえ | desk |
| いす | chair |
| たな | shelf |
| うえ | above |
| した | below |
| となり | next-to |
| あります | exist-inanimate |
| います | exist-animate |
| ふうとう | envelope |
| なか | inside |
| に | location marker |
| が | marks the thing/person whose presence is stated |
| も | also; too |
| うしろ | behind; back |
| わたし | I; me |
| はい | yes |

The delivered room diagram distinguishes the desk, shelf, chair and bag. Use the scene images at the point of discovery; the English meanings help you decode the spatial phrases without revealing the search result in advance. ここにゆいがいます means “Yui is here”; つくえのうえにほんがあります means “There is a book on the desk.” A person uses います; a book or other object uses あります. Follow who is speaking when deciding what here/there refers to.
